Based on the revised impact statement it would appear the improvements in efficiency as evidenced by the Rockville example may be limited due to other constraints, but there has been no evidence to suggest that an improvement in transportation efficiency and economy will not result from the proposed formula expansion.

Comment: Industrial development in the ring between boundaries of the present Commercial Zone of Minneapolis-St. Paul and the proposed 15 mile zone would have extremely serious adverse environmental consequences in such areas as water bodies and water courses, ground water recharge areas, wet lands, soils, agricultural lands, and unique or endangered plants and animals. (Lakeville.)
Response: Based on the available evidence, it would appear that expansion of the commercial zone will not encourage urban sprawl (see comment above). Furthermore, the anticipated adverse effects predicted by Lakeville would not occur as a direct result of this action. Expansion of industrial and commercial activity into undeveloped areas can and should be controlled by appropriate land use constraints.
